hook: Milchanowski built her career at the intersection of AI and financial crime, from model risk management at JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley to leading a global AI and quantum lab at EY that supported the U.S. National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence, before becoming BMO's first Chief AI and Quantum Officer and founding director of its applied AI institute.
name: Kristin Milchanowski

quote.text: I am honored to serve as Chief AI & Quantum Officer of BMO Financial Group and the founding Director of the BMO Institute of Applied AI & Quantum.
quote.context: Kristin Milchanowski, PhD, personal LinkedIn profile summary

moniker: Chief AI and Quantum Officer at BMO Financial Group

reading.body:
Kristin Milchanowski's career maps a single, consistent arc: applying quantitative and AI methods to financial crime and compliance risk inside large institutions, then codifying that experience into enterprise strategy.

Her timeline spans three major financial and professional-services firms before BMO, each role building on the last. Model risk management at JPMorgan fed into compliance data science at Morgan Stanley, which fed into applied research at EY that reached a national-security audience. That progression matters for AI specifically because financial crime detection is one of the highest-stakes, most data-intensive domains in banking, where model failures carry regulatory and legal consequences. The work is not experimental, it is production AI under scrutiny, which shapes how a practitioner thinks about governance, risk, and institutional accountability.

The data does not cover infrastructure, compute spend, or how BMO's AI institute is resourced. It says nothing about the scale of systems she has overseen or whether quantum computing at BMO has moved beyond strategy into deployment. What it does establish is an unusually long institutional pedigree in governed AI, and a 2026 book that frames enterprise AI adoption as a question of organizational return rather than raw capability. Whether that framing influences how banks approach the compute and power investments underlying AI scaling is not something this data addresses.
